notes: As-of 2026-09-25. All three assemblies still on their 2023 house (no fresh general election since; not in the 2024-26 election cycle list). Mizoram (9th, Dec 2023 result): 1 by-election (Dampa, MNF-held seat, MLA died 2025-07-21, successor elected 2025-11-14, no party change) applied on top of the verified 2023 constituency-results table; party-wise strength unchanged at ZPM 27/MNF 10/BJP 2/INC 1. Nagaland (14th, Mar 2023 result): current-members table on the Nagaland_Legislative_Assembly wiki page already reflects two major consolidations -- NCP Nagaland unit members switching to NDPP (2023-24) and then the landmark NDPP-into-NPF merger dated 19-21 Oct 2025 (cross-checked against the NDPP party page and Neiphiu Rio's own infobox, which now shows NPF 2025-present) -- plus 2 by-elections (Tapi Dec 2023, Koridang 2026; exact Koridang by-election date not given by source, so that holder's `since`/confidence is set low/medium). Current strength: NPF 34, BJP 12, NPP 5, IND 5, LJP(RV) 2, RPI(A) 2 = 60 (NPF absorbing ex-NDPP seats is the big change vs the pre-existing states-mz-nl-tr.json entity stats, which predate the Oct 2025 merger and should be treated as stale). Tripura (13th, Mar 2023 result): verified via the 'Results by constituency' table on 2023 Tripura Legislative Assembly election + the dedicated 'List of by-elections to the Tripura Legislative Assembly' page (4 by-elections: Boxanagar and Dhanpur both 2023-09-05, Ramnagar 2024-04-19, Dharmanagar 2026-05-04). Only Boxanagar changed party (CPI(M)->BJP, seat's original MLA died); the other three by-elections were same-party replacements. Result: BJP 33, TMP 13, CPI(M) 10, INC 3, IPFT 1 = 60, cross-checked against the '13th Tripura Assembly' wiki page's own party-wise-distribution table (exact match). Tafajjal Hossain (Boxanagar, BJP) has no Wikipedia page yet (confirmed redlink) so `holder.wikipedia` is omitted for that one position; every other one of the 160 positions has a live (non-redlink) Wikipedia URL, confirmed via the `class=new` redlink check on each source table. No vacant seats found in any of the three assemblies as of 2026-09-25. All three states have no Legislative Council (unicameral). Party abbreviations normalized to the SCHEMA's style: ZPM/MNF for Mizoram's long-form party names.

criticalCrossSegmentFinding.issue: st-mz-assembly, st-nl-assembly, st-tr-assembly are each defined as entities in BOTH this file and data/raw/states-mz-nl-tr.json, with DIFFERENT stats.partyWiseStrength.
criticalCrossSegmentFinding.detail: states-mz-nl-tr.json's Nagaland entity carries the stale AS-ELECTED Feb-2023 tally (NDPP 25, BJP 12, NPP 5, NCP 7, LJP(RV) 2, NPF 2, RPI(A) 2, JD(U) 1, Independent 4) with its own notes admitting it could not get an updated post-realignment whip list; its Tripura entity likewise carries the pre-Boxanagar-by-election tally (BJP 32, CPI(M) 11 instead of 33/10). This file's tallies (verified above, current as of 2026-09-25) are correct.
criticalCrossSegmentFinding.whyItMatters: scripts/build-graph.ts mergeInto() has no OWNER_HINTS entry for st-<code>-assembly ids, so when the two segments collide it falls back to a richness-count heuristic (richer record wins as 'base'; shallow fill-empty-fields-only for the loser) rather than a deep merge. states-mz-nl-tr.json's assembly entities carry ~6-8 more populated fields (parentId, abbr, description, legalBasis, officialUrl, headPositionId, notes) than this segment's, so richness(states) > richness(mlas)+2 regardless of file read order, meaning states-mz-nl-tr.json wins as 'base' and its stale stats object is kept whole (stats is non-empty in both, so the fill-if-empty rule never lets this segment's correct stats through). Net effect: the compiled graph will likely show the WRONG, stale party-wise strength for all three assemblies (including a NDPP party that structurally no longer holds any seats) even though this segment's own file is fully correct.
criticalCrossSegmentFinding.recommendation: Same class of problem already flagged in STATE.md for states-pb-hr-ch / states-pb-hr-ch-r2. Needs a human/critic call: either patch states-mz-nl-tr.json's three assembly stats+notes to match this file's current tallies, or add an OWNER_HINTS entry so mlas-* (or a dedicated legislature-strength segment) is authoritative for assembly partyWiseStrength. Not fixed here — out of scope for this file and not this segment's data to own.
criticalCrossSegmentFinding.severity: high — silently wrong data in the published graph if unaddressed, despite this segment being correct
